lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: What have you got for lunch?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: I've got a chicken sandwich and an apple.
lines.spa: Tengo un sándwich de pollo y una manzana.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: How often do you have a sandwich for lunch?
lines.spa: ¿Con qué frecuencia comes un sándwich en el almuerzo?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Twice a week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: What do you usually drink?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: I usually drink water.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: When do you make your packed lunch?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: In the morning, before school.
lines.spa: Por la mañana, antes de ir a la escuela.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: What do you usually put in it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: A sandwich, some fruit and a bottle of water.
lines.spa: Un sándwich, fruta y una botella de agua.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Do you ever take junk food?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: No, I don't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: What do you usually eat for breakfast?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: I usually have toast and fruit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: What do you drink?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: I drink milk.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: How often do you have eggs?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Once a week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: What do you usually have for dinner?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: We usually have rice, vegetables and chicken.
lines.spa: Normalmente comemos arroz, verduras y pollo.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Do you cook dinner?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: No, I don't. My dad usually cooks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Does he cook every day?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Yes, he does.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Do you cook at school?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Yes, I do. I'm the school cook.
lines.spa: Sí. Soy el cocinero de la escuela.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Do you read cookbooks?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Yes, I do. I read them for ideas.
lines.spa: Sí. Los leo para buscar ideas.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: What do you cook most often?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: I often cook pasta and vegetables.
lines.spa: A menudo cocino pasta y verduras.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: What's your favourite takeaway food?
lines.spa: ¿Cuál es tu comida para llevar favorita?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: I love vegetable curry.
lines.spa: Me encanta el curry de verduras.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: How often do you have it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: About once a month.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Where do you get it from?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: From a small restaurant near my house.
lines.spa: En un restaurante pequeño cerca de mi casa.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Where is pasta from?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: It's from Italy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: What about fish and chips?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: It's a famous British dish.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Are French fries from France?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Not originally. Food names can be surprising!
lines.spa: No originalmente. ¡Los nombres de comidas pueden sorprender!

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: What do you do with leftover food?
lines.spa: ¿Qué haces con la comida que sobra?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: We keep it in the fridge and eat it the next day.
lines.spa: La guardamos en la heladera y la comemos al día siguiente.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Do you throw food away?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Only when we can't use it safely.
lines.spa: Solo cuando no podemos usarla de forma segura.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: How can we reduce food waste?
lines.spa: ¿Cómo podemos reducir el desperdicio de alimentos?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: We can buy only what we need and use leftovers.
lines.spa: Podemos comprar solo lo que necesitamos y aprovechar las sobras.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Do dolphins live alone?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: No, they don't. They live in groups called pods.
lines.spa: No. Viven en grupos llamados manadas o pods.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Do sharks sleep like humans?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Not exactly. Some sharks rest while they keep moving.
lines.spa: No exactamente. Algunos tiburones descansan mientras siguen moviéndose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: What do blue whales eat?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: They eat huge amounts of small sea animals.
lines.spa: Comen enormes cantidades de pequeños animales marinos.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: What would you like in your sandwich?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Chicken, lettuce and tomato, please.
lines.spa: Pollo, lechuga y tomate, por favor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Would you like a drink?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: Yes, a fruit juice, please.
lines.spa: Sí, un jugo de frutas, por favor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.eng: Anything else?

lines.speaker: B
lines.eng: No, thank you.

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Mia takes a packed lunch to school four days a week. She usually has a chicken and tomato sandwich, an apple and a bottle of water. On Fridays, she buys lunch at school. She likes the vegetable pasta, but she doesn't eat the mushroom soup because she doesn't like mushrooms. Mia prepares her packed lunch in the morning before school.

questions.q: How often does Mia take a packed lunch?
What does she usually have in her packed lunch?
questions.a: A chicken and tomato sandwich, an apple and water
options: A chicken and tomato sandwich, an apple and water

questions.q: Why doesn't she eat the mushroom soup?
When does she prepare her lunch?

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Mr Green is the cook at River School. He starts work early and makes lunch for hundreds of students. He reads cookbooks and talks to students about their favourite meals. He often cooks pasta, rice, chicken and fresh vegetables. He doesn't serve the same meal every day, and he rarely makes very spicy food. He says the students' favourite meal is macaroni and cheese.

questions.q: What is Mr Green's job?
Does he read cookbooks?
Does he serve the same meal every day?
What meal is very popular with the students?

READING_COMPREHENSION.category: Culture and Skills - Takeaway Food in Britain
READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Takeaway food is very popular in Britain, and many favourite dishes have international influences. People often order Indian, Chinese or Italian-style food, but the British versions are not always exactly the same as dishes from those countries. Some well-known names can be misleading: a dish may have a foreign name but a different history. This shows how food changes when cultures meet.

questions.q: Is takeaway food popular in Britain?
What cuisines are mentioned?
Are British versions always identical to dishes from other countries?
What can happen when cultures meet?

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: My favourite dish is a vegetable pancake. It has flour, eggs, milk, onion and a little cheese. I usually eat it for dinner, about twice a month. My family makes it at home, so it is always fresh. I like it because it is simple, warm and delicious.

questions.q: What is the favourite dish?
What ingredients does it have?
questions.a: Flour, eggs, milk, onion and cheese
options: Flour, eggs, milk, onion and cheese

questions.q: How often does the person eat it?
Why does the person like it?
questions.a: It is simple, warm and delicious
options: It is simple, warm and delicious

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Sea animals have very different habits. Dolphins are mammals and often live in groups called pods. They communicate with sounds and can work together. Some sharks do not sleep in the same way humans do; they may rest while they keep moving. Fish often stay in schools because being in a group can give protection. Blue whales are gigantic mammals and need large amounts of food.

questions.q: What kind of animals are dolphins?
What is a group of dolphins called?
Why do fish stay in schools?
Are blue whales small animals?

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Leo's family tries not to waste food. Before shopping, they check what is already in the fridge. They buy only what they need. If there is extra cooked food, they keep it safely and use it in another meal. Sometimes they freeze food for later. At restaurants, they ask for a box when they cannot finish their meal.

questions.q: What do they do before shopping?
Do they buy more than they need?
What do they sometimes do with extra food?
options: They put it in a school bag
They throw it in the sea

questions.q: What do they ask for at restaurants?

READING_COMPREHENSION.readingText: Tom usually has an egg, toast and fruit juice for breakfast. For lunch, he has a sandwich with chicken, lettuce and tomato. He drinks water with lunch. For dinner, he often has rice with vegetables and fish. He doesn't eat junk food every day, but he sometimes has ice cream at the weekend.

questions.q: What does Tom have for breakfast?
questions.a: An egg, toast and fruit juice
options: An egg, toast and fruit juice

questions.q: What is in his lunch sandwich?

Does he eat junk food every day?
